  • .pth, sitecustomize.py, usercustomize.py, PEP 517 build hooks: not present in the provided file list.
  • ai_rulez/__init__.py: contains only __version__ = "4.0.8" and shows no import-time side effects.

Theft / Exfiltration / Persistence / Lateral Movement / Obfuscation

  • Credential harvesting: no evidence of broad discovery of environment variables, .env files, SSH keys, cloud/CI tokens, wallets, kubeconfig, or similar secrets.
  • Exfiltration: no code identified that uploads data to webhooks, raw IPs, paste services, or other suspicious endpoints.
  • Archive handling: downloader.py uses zipfile and tarfile, but the logic appears to extract a CLI binary downloaded from GitHub Releases. There is no evidence of compressing or staging harvested files.
  • Persistence: no cron, systemd, launch agent, shell profile modification, background polling loop, or self-reinstall logic was identified.
  • Lateral movement: no evidence involving Kubernetes, Docker socket access, cloud metadata, GitHub Actions token abuse, or registry token reuse.
  • Obfuscation/loaders: no evidence of eval/exec, base64/zlib/marshal obfuscation, staged loaders, or self-deleting droppers.

Distribution Integrity Anomalies

  • The PyPI sdist contains only the Python wrapper and metadata; no unexplained native binary or hidden payload is visible in the provided file list.
  • downloader.py downloads a platform-specific binary from GitHub Releases and verifies checksums when the user runs the ai-rulez CLI. This is worth validating from a supply-chain perspective, but the provided evidence does not show it is malicious.
  • install_requires=[]; no suspicious dependency insertion was observed.
  • No evidence suggesting typosquatting or dependency confusion was identified.
